{"description":"THE ONE ORDER for the work left in two plans, on @ajs's word from the dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-09-27: "I want this to be captured as an epoch/increment in reflow2" (asked twice on 2026-09-26 and twice on 2026-09-27). It combines:
- flo2's plan from Alex's list of 2026-09-26 (Hub; sharing easily via flo2; running reflow2 remotely over MCP; connecting via Grok Build; flo2 backups; configurable reflow2 backups), held in flo2's design;
- reflow2's tracked-export retirement plan (steps 1 to 8, confirmed 2026-09-27) and its two tracks outside that order;
- and, added later the same night on @ajs's word ("yes, record it and schedule group 1"), two flo2.io increments from flo2's dec:the-seventeen-tools-api-flo2-io-withholds-and-what-brings-each-back.

EACH INCREMENT STAYS IN THE DESIGN THAT OWNS IT; this epoch holds only the order across them. An increment's position is also in its own name ("[Combined N]") so either design read alone shows it. The names carry no total, so adding an increment renumbers only what follows it.

═══ THE ORDER ═══
1. The hosted engine closes idle designs, says busy when full, keeps a memory budget, and drains before it stops — reflow2, epoch:planned-the-hosted-engine-closes-idle-designs-and-drains. Idle close (#605) and the memory budget (#606) are merged; draining on stop is built, not yet merged.
2. api.flo2.io offers the five file-evidence tools (link_artifact, set_artifact_checksum(s), reconcile_artifacts, coverage_report) with the caller's own evidence — flo2, epoch:api-flo2-io-offers-the-file-evidence-tools. Group 1 of the seventeen-tools decision; a flo2-only change.
3. A code folder names the design it implements and its server — reflow2, epoch:planned-a-code-folder-names-its-design (tracked-export step 3). Finishes Alex's item 3 on reflow2's side.
4. A hub is a named list of a person's designs — flo2, epoch:a-hub-is-a-named-list. Alex's item 1, minimal form.
5. A person shares a design with another account themselves — flo2, epoch:self-serve-sharing. Alex's item 2. It STARTS by settling how sharing works (flo2's dec:idea-choose-which-account-to-share-a-design-with: Alex's email invite or @ajs's share link), which is @ajs's to decide.
6. A shared hub — flo2, epoch:shared-hubs. Alex's item 1, full form. After 5.
7. The client measures a folder's own files for a design on a server — reflow2, epoch:planned-local-files-are-measured-for-a-remote-design (step 4). After 3. Also where group 2 of the seventeen-tools decision returns (wall_check, reconcile_dependencies, ingest_corpus_step).
8. A branch's implementation facts live in the store — reflow2, epoch:planned-branch-facts-live-in-the-store (step 5).
9. CI checks the code against its design on the server — reflow2, epoch:planned-ci-asks-the-blueprint (step 6). After 7 and 8.
10. A release cut works against a design on a server — reflow2, epoch:planned-a-release-cut-works-against-a-remote-design (step 7). After 7.
11. flo2's design moves to a server, then reflow2's; the tracked export retires — reflow2, epoch:planned-flo2-then-reflow2-move-and-the-photocopy-retires (step 8). After 9 and 10.
12. A design on flo2.io is compared, merged, certified and replaced against another design without a path on the host — flo2, epoch:a-hosted-design-works-with-another-design-without-a-host-path. Group 3 of the seventeen-tools decision; its route is not chosen and its requirement is proposed. Placed last because nothing waits on it.
THE ONLY HARD DEPENDENCIES are the "after" clauses. Every other adjacency is preference and may be swapped without re-planning anything else (e.g. 3 before 2).

═══ OUTSIDE THE ORDER ═══
- Backups without stopping the server — reflow2, epoch:planned-backups-without-stopping-the-server. Relates to Alex's item 5. Measured 2026-09-27: most of the nightly backup's ~10 s pause is Docker's stop timeout against a process 1 with no SIGTERM handler, which position 1's drain removes.
- Alex's item 6, "configurable reflow2 backups" — NOT CAPTURED. Its meaning is still to be settled with Alex before it becomes a requirement.
- Group 4 of the seventeen-tools decision (writes_for, sync_status) stays off api.flo2.io by design.

═══ ALREADY DELIVERED FROM THE TWO PLANS ═══
- Technical agents reach flo2 directly (api.flo2.io, personal keys, the Grok Build and Claude Code routes) — flo2, arrived 2026-09-26. Alex's items 3 (flo2's side) and 4. Claude Code's browser sign-in measured working on 2026-09-27 (flo2's fact:claude-code-signs-in-to-api-flo2-io-in-the-browser-and-works-storyflow-2026-09-28).
- Every nightly backup also lands off-site, encrypted, with a real restore proven — flo2, epoch:off-site-backups, arrived 2026-09-26 (flo2 #80, #81). Alex's item 5.
- The remote client and its setup command released as v0.72.0 — reflow2 step 1, arrived 2026-09-27. Alex's item 3 (reflow2's side).
- A design watched at the server that holds it, shipped in v0.72.0 — reflow2 step 2, arrived 2026-09-27.

This epoch ARRIVES when the last increment in the order does.
